Find Construct Body

dot-find_construct_body.Rd

Locate the body expression of a construct (if, else, for, while, repeat, function or lambda \(x)) in the parse data of the checked code, for the construction of the modified function by curly_bracket_check. The body is the last expr child of the construct expression: for if, the condition expr comes first, the then body follows, and the else body (if any) is the last expr child; for for, the forcond (which owns the parentheses) comes before the body expr; for while, repeat, function and lambdas, the body is also the last expr child.

Usage

.find_construct_body(
  pd,
  kid,
  body_start,
  body_start_pos,
  term_rows,
  else_branch,
  else_tok,
  intern_error_text_start,
  intern_error_text_end,
  lib_path,
  error_text
)

Arguments

pd

Data frame returned by utils::getParseData() on the code of the checked function.

kid

Single integer: row index in pd of the terminal token of the construct keyword (IF, FOR, WHILE, REPEAT, FUNCTION, LAMBDA or '\\').

body_start

Single integer: row index in pd of the terminal token just before the body (the closing ) of the condition or of the arguments, or the keyword itself for repeat).

body_start_pos

Single integer: position in term_rows of the terminal token body_start.

term_rows

Integer vector of the terminal rows (comments excluded) of pd, sorted by source position (as computed in curly_bracket_check).

else_branch

Single logical value. Is the requested body the else branch of the if() construct? If TRUE, the last expr child of the construct expression is returned; if FALSE, the then body of an if with an else (the second-to-last expr child) is returned.

else_tok

Single integer or NULL: row index in pd of the ELSE token (used only when else_branch = TRUE, for the internal error messages).

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A list with: row, row index in pd of the body expr (whose col1/line1 give the position just before the body, and col2/line2 the position of the last character of the body); line1, the line of the body start; col1, the column (character offset) of the body start.

Details

Warnings:

  • requires saferDev::arg_check.

  • In the safer Backbone section "######## check of the required functions from the required packages", add also saferDev::arg_check when checking for the presence of .find_construct_body.
